trigger: drain_log_bounded() (not noexcept) sat unguarded, after agent->run() returns, immediately before the "an explicit operator stop always wins" report_status() chain in service_win.cpp
summary: An uncaught exception there would skip the operator-stop-wins report_status() branch and fall into the outer catch blocks, misreporting a clean operator-initiated stop as SERVICE_STOPPED/specific=3, which under --install-service's SERVICE_CONFIG_FAILURE_ACTIONS_FLAG risks an unwanted SC_ACTION_RESTART of the device the operator just stopped. Independently found by cpp-safety and unhappy-path (UP-2). Fixed by wrapping the call in its own try/catch(...).

trigger: a sink-level write failure coinciding with a blocked/backpressured stderr (full pipe, stalled log collector)
summary: The new rate-limited stderr fallback held error_state->mu across an unbounded std::fprintf/std::fflush(stderr). A stuck stderr at the moment of a sink failure would block the async logger's one worker thread (or a producer thread) while holding the lock, serializing every future log_errors_total()/last_log_error_for_test() caller and future handler invocations behind it, with no timeout outside the shutdown-time watchdog. Independently found by cpp-safety and unhappy-path in the same wording/mechanism. Fixed by snapshotting the fields to emit under the lock, then doing the stderr I/O after releasing it.

trigger: the Linux-confirmed/Windows-inferred/macOS-measured-two-registries correction landed in only some of the files stating the same fact
summary: log_handoff.hpp's file banner was broadened in pass 1 but its separate MULTI-IMAGE doc-comment further down the same file, plus a test-file top comment and a second untouched spot in server-admin.md, still called macOS topology "unproved" and Windows registry-sharing flatly "confirmed." Independently found by cpp-safety, docs-writer, and consistency-auditor. All four locations corrected to the same Linux-confirmed/Windows-inferred/macOS-measured framing.

trigger: a reader compares the stderr-fallback comment's parity claim, or the flush_on(warn) comment's mechanism claim, against the actual code/spdlog behavior
summary: The stderr fallback's comment claimed "strict superset, never a reduction" of spdlog's default handler, but the emitted line omits the timestamp/logger-name fields the default includes. The flush_on(warn) comment claimed a second queued flush entry; verified against vendored spdlog 1.17.0 source that it is an inline synchronous flush on the same worker callback with no extra queue slot. Independently found by sre, cpp-expert, and security-guardian. Both comments corrected.

trigger: a transient (self-healing) exception during the exe-image logger-registry swap on Linux/Windows, where a later teardown step nulls the same shared registry regardless

Code behavior itself not changed -- this is a doc-precision fix, not a design change to the fail-closed gate.
